---
title: "Get Started"
subtitle: "What do you need to know to start using animovement? Learn what you need in 5 articles."
toc: false
---

*animovement* is a family of R packages for movement data analysis. 
Each package owns one stage of the analysis, and they all speak the same
data structure — the **aniframe** — so the output of one stage is the input to
the next, with nothing to convert in between.

These five articles take you along that arc, from installing the ecosystem to
speed, heading and distance travelled, using one recording throughout. Work
through them in order — each builds on the last. Once you have the basics,
[Learn](../learn/index.qmd) is where you go further.

::: {.callout-note}
## New to R or the tidyverse?
To get the most out of *animovement*, we recommend starting with the basics of
R and the [tidyverse](https://www.tidyverse.org) first — the
[Posit primers](https://posit.cloud/learn/primers),
[R for Data Science](https://r4ds.hadley.nz) or
[ModernDive](https://moderndive.com) are all good places to begin.
*animovement* is tidyverse-friendly: aniframes are tibbles, so `dplyr`,
`tidyr` and `ggplot2` work on them as they do on any other data.
:::
